capabilities.target: Agent memory store, injected into future session system prompts
Any external email address, via the user's mailbox
User's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start and injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Memory content is trusted purely by instruction, with no structural provenance tagging, review, or trust separation enforced outside the model.
Recalled memories are unconditionally granted the authority of 'the user's own instructions' regardless of their actual origin, including origin in untrusted web content.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) on mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, though it can be removed by its owner (control_removal) or bypassed if autonomy increases past the gate.

controls.name: Memory write provenance tagging and trust gating
controls.decay_rationale: If enforced at the memory store rather than by the model, provenance tags block untrusted content from later being recalled as trusted instructions regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scoped to only task-relevant documents does not decay with model capability; the model cannot read what it has no access to.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to system-of-record contacts
controls.decay_rationale: Does not decay because the destination comes from the system of record rather than from model output.

controls.name: Network and recipient egress allowlist
controls.decay_rationale: An allowlist that excludes attacker-controlled destinations does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Remove instruction that elevates recalled memory to trusted status
controls.decay_rationale: Even if added, a behavioral instruction not to trust memory depends on model compliance and would weaken under model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon; it is a stopgap, not a substitute for ctrl.memory_provenance.

findings.title: Memory laundering of untrusted web content into trusted instructions, escalating to confidential data exfiltration (TC5 into TC1)

attack_path.note: A fetched web page contains content framed as the user's preferences or standing instructions.
Following prompt.md lines 2-3, the agent saves this web-sourced content via memory.save with no provenance tagging and no user review.
The entry persists with no distinction between user-authored and web-sourced content (runtime notes).
At the next session start the entry is recalled and, per prompt.md line 4, treated as the user's own instruction.
The now-trusted 'instruction' directs the agent to read confidential files from the user's full drive.
The agent sends the retrieved confidential content to an address the injected content specified, with no approval step.

forecast.watch_signal: Already at the ceiling with zero credited controls; watch for new memory-fed data sources or a model upgrade, which would make exploitation more reliable even though the tier cannot rise further.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to save anything useful about user preferences or standing instructions via memory.save, with no restriction on the source of that content.
Instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every session, with no verification of origin.
memory.save accepts free text with no provenance, and entries are never reviewed by the user before being injected into the next session's system prompt.

mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive of confidential files, so a laundered memory instruction can trigger an unreviewed, irreversible exfiltration.

recommendations.action: Add provenance tagging to memory.save so entries derived from untrusted web content are never recalled as trusted instructions (ctrl.memory_provenance).
Require raw-action human approval before mail.send, with the recipient bound to a system-of-record contact list (ctrl.email_approval_gate, ctrl.email_recipient_binding).

Remove the system prompt instruction that tells the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions (ctrl.no_implicit_trust_instruction); treat this as a stopgap, not a substitute for structural provenance.

findings.title: Same-session lethal trifecta: untrusted research content, confidential drive read, and unapproved email send (TC1)

attack_path.note: A fetched web page contains injected instructions, encountered while the agent also holds drive.read and mail.send in the same session.
The agent reads confidential files from the user's full drive, as directed by the injected content.
The agent sends the confidential content to an attacker-specified address via mail.send with no approval step.

forecast.watch_signal: Already at the ceiling with zero credited controls; watch for new egress-capable tools or a model upgrade, which would make the injection more reliable even though the tier cannot rise further.

evidence.observation: mail.send, drive.read, and the web-fetching research function are all capabilities of the single research-assistant agent, so content encountered during research shares context with the ability to read confidential files and send email in the same session.
mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files, with no approval gate anywhere in the design.

The agent's job is to research topics (fetch and read web content, an untrusted source) and draft emails, placing untrusted content, drive read, and email send together with no isolation between them.

recommendations.action: Scope drive.read to least-privilege, task-relevant documents rather than the full drive (ctrl.drive_scope).
Gate mail.send behind raw-action human approval and a recipient egress allowlist (ctrl.email_approval_gate, ctrl.egress_allowlist).

rating.rationale: The design has no structural controls anywhere on the paths from untrusted web content to confidential drive data to unapproved, irreversible email send. Untrusted content can reach that sink directly within a single research session, and it can also be laundered into memory and re-injected as 'the user's own instructions' in every future session (prompt.md line 4), with no provenance, review, or approval at any point (runtime notes). Both paths compute to a critical inherent risk (untrusted source, severe egress sink) and, because every mitigating control is absent (status missing_recommended, earning no credit), residual risk remains critical with no reduction. Forecast stays critical because the tier is already at the ceiling; the highest-priority fixes are a raw-action human approval gate on mail.send and provenance tagging on memory writes, which together would narrow or sever both paths.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or agent card was provided; capability scope (for example, the exact extent of drive.read or email send semantics) is inferred from the runtime notes, which limits confidence to medium for the direct same-session injection finding.

No autonomy or runtime configuration artifact was provided; autonomy level, step limits, and the first-party trust domain were inferred from the absence of any stated approval gates, step bounds, or deployment ownership information.
